newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Manuli Rubber, to be listed, sees good 97.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Manuli Rubber, to be listed, sees good 97.

text.p: Italy's Manuli Rubber, which on Monday ended a roadshow ahead of its Milan stock market listing, said it posted higher sales and profit in the first four months and sees full year results up on 1996.
Manuli saw turnover rise 10.4 percent to 149.3 billion lire ($87.9 million) and operating profit up 14.4 percent to 23.9 billion.
"For full year 1997 we expect better results than 1996 and in line with growth in the first four months," said managing director Aldo Occari.
The company, offering a total 26 million shares on July 7 and 8 at a price of between 4,850 and 5,650 lire per share, said it aimed to expand and make new acquisitions.
The multinational group makes rubber tubes, couplings and assemblies for fluid transmission in auto and hydraulic applications.
After the share placement of 28.2 percent on the market, the Manuli family stake will fall to 71.78 percent from 82.55 percent currently.
The company posted 1996 net profit of 37.6 billion lire, against 36.8 billion, on net turnover 382.2 billion against 395.2 billion. It said turnover was hurt by exchange rate fluctutations.
"One of the main reasons behind the bourse listing is to continue growing, also with new acquisitions," said chairman Mario Manuli.

"We are aiming to take control of our 33 percent owned unit Murray Europe, the main supplier to Fiat and Saab of flexible tubing for air conditioning and servo-steering systems, and we will make an offer for an east European company," he added without elaborating.
